knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes the variable-selection decision and the role of model-fit measures?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Selection compares candidate explanatory sets using fit measures with complexity penalties. Mechanical p-value chopping and GLM conflation are wrong tasks.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Select explanatory set via fit measures; more variables is not automatically better.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Mechanical p-value chopping or conflating linear selection with GLM link-and-family modelling.

choices.label: Select an appropriate set of explanatory variables using fit measures that reward fit while penalising unnecessary complexity. More explanatory variables is not automatically better because overfitting and diluted interpretation can worsen the model.
Keep every term with p less than 0.05; that mechanical rule completes explanatory-variable selection.
Variable selection for linear models is the same task as choosing a GLM link function; both are finished by raw R-squared alone.
The best explanatory set always contains every available numeric column because unused columns waste information.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Two nested linear models for claim severity: M1 uses age only; M2 adds sum insured and NCD. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Name fit measures; refuse p-chopping and GLM conflation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Adjusted R-squared and AIC/BIC penalise complexity. p-value chopping and GLM conflation do not finish linear explanatory selection.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Adjusted R-squared; AIC/BIC. Refuse p-chopping and GLM conflation.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting p-value chopping or treating selection as finishing GLM.

choices.label: Examples: adjusted R-squared (rewards fit while adjusting for unused complexity versus raw R-squared); AIC or BIC (likelihood fit with a parameter-count penalty). Mechanical p-value chopping is not a complete selection warrant; GLM uses links and exponential-family responses, not linear explanatory selection alone.
Keep every term with p less than 0.05 in M2 and selection is done; no fit measure comparison is needed.
Variable selection finishes GLM modelling because both choose predictors using software output.
Raw R-squared alone decides between M1 and M2 because it never increases when variables are added.
